title: Traffic-aware cohort curation for quantization validation
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a production-oriented curation pipeline that constructs calibration cohorts ("packs") for FP8/INT8 quantization validation. Unlike simple per-domain packs, this task focuses on traffic-aware cohort construction: weighting recent production prompts, capping per-customer influence, preserving rare intents, and producing small deterministic packs suitable for offline quantization runs and continuous regression checks. The packs should be privacy-conscious (hashed identifiers, differential sampling), reproducible, and annotated for sequence-length buckets and attention/kernel sensitivity.

Goals:
- Produce compact calibration cohorts (~2k-10k prompts per pack) representative of current traffic and sensitive subpopulations (rare intents, long sequences, high-token-rate prompts).
- Ensure packs expose accuracy regressions when switching between FP8/INT8 quantization profiles or kernel variants.
- Limit per-customer and per-tenant dominance via capped weighting and reservoir constraints.
- Maintain reproducibility (seeded RNG) and explainability (sampling provenance metadata).

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline can generate N=5 domain/cohort packs for a rollout candidate in <30 minutes from aggregated logs (after pre-aggregation).
- Packs detect quality regressions introduced by two experimental FP8 kernels with >90% of known-regression probes failing sanity thresholds in prior test cases.
- Privacy controls: no raw customer identifiers in pack artifacts, and per-customer contribution capped at 0.5% by default.
- Integration: packs usable by existing offline quantization harness (runtime-1.21) without schema changes.

Proposed sampling algorithm (high level):
1) Pre-aggregation: nightly job aggregates production prompts into pre-buckets with metadata (domain, tenant_hash, intent_hash, seq_len, token_count, timestamp, latency). Raw prompt text is only retained in encrypted blob accessible to authorized validation jobs; export artifacts use prompt_id referencing vaulted storage.
2) Freshness weighting: apply exponential decay weight w(t)=exp(-lambda * age_days). Default lambda tuned to half-life=14 days. This biases cohorts to recent traffic but preserves a long tail for rare intents.
3) Intent stratification: identify top-K intents per domain (by weighted volume) and create explicit strata for top-K, medium, and rare intents. Rare intents get an upweight factor (configurable) to ensure coverage.
4) Per-tenant capping: compute contribution share per tenant after weighting; if any tenant > cap (default 0.5%), downsample deterministically using a seeded reservoir sample to meet cap.
5) Sequence-length and latency buckets: enforce minimum counts in short (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), and long (>512) buckets; ensure high-latency tail (>p95) prompts are present as 3% of pack.
6) Edge-case anchors: include a curated list of ~200 anchor prompts derived from prior regressions and fuzzed paraphrases (perturbations) to increase sensitivity to quant-induced errors.
7) Dedup fingerprinting: use a rolling-token-hash (k-shingle, k=5) to deduplicate near-duplicates while preserving paraphrase diversity. Keep at most N_similar=3 paraphrases per fingerprint group.
8) Privacy step: replace tenant_id with salted hash and drop any prompt-level PII tags found by the PII detector; produce a provenance file listing sampling seeds and filter steps.
9) Output: pack JSONL with prompt_id (vault ref), domain, intent_bucket, seq_len_bucket, weight, sample_seed, fingerprint_id, and a compact validation-context (first 2 tokens + last 2 tokens) for quick eyeballing.

Operational considerations:
- Performance: pre-aggregation should reduce candidate set to <1M/day to keep sampling job <30m.
- Determinism: all sampling uses explicit RNG seeds stored with the pack metadata so experiments are reproducible.
- Storage: packs stored in S3 path: s3://redwood-calibration/packs/{release}/{yyyy-mm-dd}/{pack-name}.jsonl.gz with accompanying metadata JSON.
- Cost: provide an estimate of offline validation compute cost per pack (tokens x model variants).

Validation plan:
- Unit tests for weighting and capping logic (edge-cases: single tenant dominating, bursty rare intent).
- Integration test: generate pack and run existing quantization regression harness; measure detection rate against baseline FP32->INT8 regressions from historical incident set.
- A/B run: for one dedicated batch, run FP8 candidate and baseline on the pack and generate differential metric report (per-example logprob deltas, token-level disagreement, semantic similarity using embedding-based scorer).

Rollout steps:
1) Merge sampling pipeline into staging cluster; generate initial packs for runtime-1.21 engineers and PM reviewers.
2) Run regression harness, collect signal, iterate thresholds.
3) Add pack generation to weekly scheduled job with configurable domains and rare-intent upweighting.
4) Document usage in Console: allow engineers to download pack metadata and re-run locally.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Over-upweighting rare intents may cause packs that are less reflective of actual production error surface; counter by capping rare-intent fraction (configurable, default 8%).
- Deterministic downsampling may inadvertently bias for/against particular request shapes; mitigate with randomized seeds across runs and holdout validation.
- PII filtering complexity: false negatives are a risk; require security review before enabling text exports.

Next steps / concrete tasks:
- [ ] Implement pre-aggregation job (ENG infra task)
- [ ] Implement sampling microservice (Go) with config API and seeded RNG
- [ ] Add dedup fingerprint library (Python) and integrate with microservice
- [ ] Hook into quant regression harness and run smoke tests on 3 historical incidents
- [ ] Create Confluence doc with sampling knobs and operator runbook

Deliverables:
- Sampling microservice + CLI (Docker image + Helm chart)
- One example pack for domains: search, chat, summarization, code-assist, customer-support (each 2k-8k prompts)
- Regression report comparing FP32 baseline vs two FP8 candidates and INT8 baseline on generated packs
